new_statements.quote: [Zorc 1977:244] "Even in languages where the accent falls on a specifiable syllable of every full word, an enclitic changes the accent: Kalamian Tagbanwa bálay house + -u my → balá:yu my house." [Himes 2006:3] "Stress was also phonemic in PPh. Proto-Kalamian (PKlm) seems to have lost stress as a phonemic feature." [Zorc 1978:104 n.13] "Kalamian [mátaq]" ('eye'). [Zorc fieldnotes, Northern Tagbanwa bundle p. 9, handwritten, unpublished] "Stress not phonemic: CV́CCVC automatic"

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Primary quote CONFIRMED verbatim on the saved page image (Zorc 1977, PL C-44, p. 244, §10.2.2): "Even in languages where the accent falls on a specifiable syllable of every full word, an enclitic changes the accent: Kalamian Tagbanwa bálay house + -u my → balá:yu my house." Also confirmed on p. 218): "Palawano, Aborlan, and Agutaynen, which also do not have contrastive word accent" (Agutaynen = sister language, not cala1258 itself), and in the text layer p. 287 n. 8: Zorc gathered Kalamian Tagbanwa data independently and cross-checked it against Reid (1971). Himes 2006:3 §2 CONFIRMED verbatim in lines 74-75: "Stress was also phonemic in PPh. Proto-Kalamian (PKlm) seems to have lost stress a…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive (Himes 2006; Zorc's fieldnote 'Stress not phonemic'); per Zorc 1977 it falls on a predictable ('specifiable') syllable of every full word, which his examples show to be the penult (bálay 'house', [mátaq] 'eye'; closed penult 'CV́CCVC automatic'), and the accent moves rightward so as to stay on the penult of the word-plus-enclitic (bálay + -u → balá:yu 'my house'). No source states the syllable in so many words; 'penult' is inferred from the examples.
new_statements.exceptions: Contradictory data: Reid 1971:42 (Ruch 1959 analysis) lists 'Stress' among the phonemes of Kalamian Tagbanwa; Zorc's own handwritten 'Stress' list (bundle p. 8) marks final stress in baláy, tanán, ináy, takún, bɨlág, talagáŋ, ilə́m beside penult íyan, mangárɨn, and his PPh worksheet has kalawíd, bɨlág; Ruch 1974 omits stress from the phoneme inventory. Zorc 1977:218 says only Palawano, Aborlan and Agutaynen (sister language) lack contrastive word accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Word plus enclitic pronoun/particle forms one accentual domain (accent shifts under enclisis, Zorc 1977:244; fieldnote forms kəsəkəsán nu, bənlawán nu). Data are Zorc's field elicitations (Coron, Banwang Daan) cross-checked with Ruch's SIL data; Himes's statement is comparative, based on Reid 1971 / Quakenbush / Ruch data.
new_statements.identity_note: All first-hand data concern Kalamian Tagbanwa proper (= Northern Tagbanwa, Tinagbanwa of Coron Island / Banwang Daan), i.e. cala1258 [tbk]. Zorc's separate 'Kalamian/Kalamyanis' bundle is the Karamiananen (Busuanga/Culion) variety, a coordinate dialect of cala1258 per Himes 2006, elicited from a Kuyonon L1 speaker and not used for the reading. Zorc 1977:218's 'do not have contrastive word accent' names Agutaynen (agut1237, sister language), Palawano and Aborlan, not Kalamian Tagbanwa itself. Himes 2006's statement is about Proto-Kalamian (Agutaynen + Kalamian Tagbanwa dialects).

sources.note: Handwritten p. 9: 'Northern Tagbanwa... Stress not phonemic: CV́CCVC automatic'. p. 8 'Stress' list with mixed marks: íyan, bɨlág, mangárɨn, takún; baláy, talagáŋ, tanán, ilə́m, ináy. p. 2 text: bálay, manáyaw, durúŋan, ipakáldaw, sakbáyan; kəsəkəsán nu, bənlawán nu, pəyán da (accent on penult of word+enclitic). Typed Ruch 1959/1964 excerpts (pp. 30-39) carry no stress marks and no stress statement.
